correctness.rationale: The full ordered-density derivation yields two one-extreme boundary terms in the joint density of gap G and reciprocal range V. The local density behaves as \(g^{r-1}\), giving \(t\log(1/t)\) for adjacent ranks and t with a finite inverse-gap coefficient for separated ranks. The n=4 right endpoint follows from two endpoint-cluster simplex integration and a uniform Cauchy-product tail bound. Standalone checker confirms the explicit elementary integrals and bounded numerical comparisons; numerical checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The statistic is the natural empirical four-quantile ratio of a published Cauchy goodness-of-fit procedure. Its smallest-p-value tail changes from t log(1/t) to t depending on interior rank separation, because one Cauchy extreme competes with central spacing collapse; exact constants enable rare-tail analytical calibration for rank implementations otherwise simulated. The four-rank upper tail gives a contrasting quadratic power and sharp reciprocal-moment thresholds. This is a nontrivial fixed-sample structural calibration theorem rather than a routine renaming or parameter substitution.
